If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

page_token.description: list only: the `next_page_token` a listing of the same scope gave, to list the artifacts after it.

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (writing people will keep editing or pass around as text, such as a memo, plan, spec, proposal or notes), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a page to look at or use: an explainer, a diagram, anything interactive, a dashboard that shows data, a spreadsheet, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

browser-use <<'PY'

PY

  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

### Task 6: The Responses stream protocol, and the format goes live (spec D10–D13, § 6.5)

**Files:**
- Create: `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/src/responses/stream.rs`
- Modify: `src/types.rs` (`Format::OpenAiResponses`), `src/protocol.rs`, `src/interceptor.rs`, `src/body.rs`, `src/turn.rs`, `src/responses/*.rs` (delete every `allow(dead_code)` line)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Tasks 3, 4, 5.
- Produces:
  - `pub enum Format { OpenAiChat, AnthropicMessages, OpenAiResponses }`.
  - `protocol::Step::Terminal { frame: Frame, completed: Vec<(HoldKey, Vec<ToolCall>)> }` — the interceptor completes each listed hold, then truncates every hold still in `incomplete()`, then enqueues the frame.
  - `protocol::StepError::AfterEnd` — the interceptor counts `Metric::RecordDropped("after_done")` and drops the record, with no stream failure.
  - `Protocol::closing_on_abort(&mut self, verdicts: &Verdicts) -> Vec<Bytes>` with a default body that returns `Vec::new()`. `Interceptor::abort` emits it before the terminal frame. Chat and Anthropic keep the default, so their bytes do not change.
  - `responses::stream::ResponsesStream::with_cap(cap: usize) -> Self`, `impl Protocol`.
  - `Interceptor::new(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)`, `parse_body(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)` and `parse_request(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)` work.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** in `stream.rs` (drive `ResponsesStream` directly, as `openai/stream.rs` tests do) and in `interceptor.rs`:
  - `allow_all_reemits_every_payload_with_its_event_line` (D11): each output record is `event: <type>\ndata: <original payload>\n\n`; `[DONE]` has no `event:` line.
  - `a_blocked_function_call_becomes_a_message_at_its_index`: the `added` frame becomes exactly the three § 6.5 events, every delta frame is dropped, the `done` frame becomes the `output_item.done` message, and the terminal `output[i]` is the completed message; no byte of the blocked arguments is in the output.
  - `a_blocked_item_without_done_gets_a_synthesized_done`: before the terminal frame (release), before EOF (`closing`), and before the D13 frame (`closing_on_abort`).
  - `the_rewrite_repeats_the_sequence_number`: the three events from one `added` carry its `sequence_number`; a stream without `sequence_number` gives events without the key.
  - `a_truncated_item_blocks_the_whole_hold` (D10, R15): two client-run items, the second `done` has `status: "incomplete"`; at the terminal event both calls are blocked with `Truncated`, and the decider is not asked.
  - `frames_after_the_terminal_are_dropped_and_done_is_emitted` (R3): a text event after `response.completed` gives `StepError::AfterEnd`; `[DONE]` after it gives `Step::End`.
  - `provider_frames_wait_behind_an_open_hold` (749 D12): a `web_search_call` after an open hold is released after the decision, in stream order, with its report comment.
  - `unframed_writes_a_safe_event_line` (Review Focus 1): `unframed` of `{"type":"response.created"}` writes `event: response.created`; of `{"type":"a\nb"}`, of a 65-byte type and of a non-JSON record writes no `event:` line.
  - `known_calls_name_the_qualified_names`.
  - In `interceptor.rs`: `a_responses_stream_runs_end_to_end` (one hold, one `Decide` with every client-run call of the response, the rewrite on block), and `the_chat_abort_bytes_do_not_change` (`abort` on an OpenAI chat interceptor with a blocked, truncated choice emits only `TERMINAL`).
  - In `body.rs`: `a_responses_body_parses_and_rewrites_through_parse_body`, and the § 7.1 case `structured_output_keys_pass_on_the_body` (schema properties `Name`, `ID`, `Type`, `constructor`, metadata key `Id`, `maximum: 1e300`: `parse_body` is `Ok` and `apply` with allow returns `None`).
  - In `turn.rs`: `parse_request_reads_a_responses_request`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `CORE`. Expected: FAIL.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `step` calls `classify`, then `Assembly::accept` for `Known` events; `Terminal` comes from a terminal event (with `completed = [(HoldKey::Response, hold_calls())]` only when the hold is open and not truncated), `End` from `[DONE]`, `UpstreamError` from an error record. Every frame of a client-run item and the terminal frame touch `HoldKey::Response`; no other frame touches anything. `release` rewrites only frames that hold a blocked item (`slot_of` + `Verdict::block_code`); every other frame keeps its payload bytes. The notice for slot `s` is `notice_line(&call.display_name(), code)`. If Task 1 recorded a wire `output_text` field in the terminal `response` (M2), add the notice to it and write that in the spec § 6.5 line that names it; otherwise do nothing. `Interceptor::new` uses `ResponsesStream::with_cap(limits.max_held_bytes)`. `parse_body` uses the Task 3 strict parse and number check for `OpenAiResponses` and the old path for the other two formats. Delete every `allow(dead_code)` line that Tasks 3–5 added.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `CORE`, `LINT`, and `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway-core --test golden` (no update). Expected: PASS, goldens unchanged. Run `grep -rn "allow(dead_code)" rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/src`. Expected: no line from this branch (`git diff origin/main -- rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/src | grep -c "allow(dead_code)"` prints `0`).
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat(rs): intercept responses streams with one hold per response (SMA-769)`.

- Exact values (copy them, do not retype them from memory):
  - Error code `responses-stateful-not-supported`, proto `ERROR_REASON_RESPONSES_STATEFUL_NOT_SUPPORTED = 314;`, HTTP 400, OpenAI type `invalid_request_error`, message `Stateful Responses API requests are not supported by this gateway.`
  - D13 frame, as a Rust literal: `"\n\nevent: error\ndata: {\"type\":\"error\",\"code\":\"upstream-error\",\"message\":\"upstream stream error\",\"param\":null}\n\n"`.
  - Rewrite id: `msg_paigasus_<i>`, with `<i>` the blocked `output_index` in decimal.
  - Responses limits: `max_record_bytes = 16_777_216` (16 MiB), `max_held_bytes = 33_554_432` (32 MiB), `[responses] max_request_bytes = 16_777_216` (16 MiB). `[responses] enabled = false` by default.

- The chat route must not change. Every existing core golden is byte-identical, and every existing service test passes. The only edit allowed in an existing test file is a new `responses: None` field in an `AppState { … }` literal (Task 11), and new test functions next to the old ones.
- A spec rule is never loosened in code. If a measurement or a test shows that real traffic breaks a § 6.4 rule or the § 6.5 rewrite, stop and report to the coordinator.

- `SVC`: `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway`

## Findings

**F1. Global Constraints forbid edits the tasks require.** Plan: "The only edit allowed in an existing test file is `responses: None` ... and new test functions." Tasks that edit existing test files otherwise: T7 (`ModelCall` fields in `tests/support/oracle.rs`), T8 (`streams.rs`), T9 (`golden.rs` `SET`, `manifest.json`, edits to existing tests in `fixtures.rs`), T10 (`RecordedRequest.path`), T14 (`tests/support/mod.rs` mock), T16 (rename of `test_manifest_lists_six_goldens`). Spec AC 8 says only that the existing tests pass. Ruling: reword the constraint: "existing tests keep their assertions; helper types and sets may grow".

**F2. The oracle reads calls from `added` for built-in kinds, but R13 lets `shell_call` `added` differ from `done`.** Plan T7 / spec § 10.1: openai-python `ResponseStream` calls come from every `output_item.added` item of kinds other than function and custom. R13: `added` and `done` differ in `action.commands`. An allowed, conforming `shell_call` then gives a model call that differs from the decided call, so P1 can fail on a good stream (T8 generates `shell_call`). Ruling: for `shell_call`, take the model call from `done` only, or require `added.action.commands` to be the decided value. Say which in T7.

**F3. Quirks do not cover every rule.** Spec § 10.3 / AC 4: "every rule of § 6.4 gets a generator quirk." The `RQuirk` list has none for R1 `first_not_created`, R3 `second_terminal`, R4 `index_order`, R6 `wrong_item_index`, R10 `terminal_output_mismatch` (partly), R11 `arguments_mismatch`, R12 `input_mismatch`, R14 `added_done_differ`, `long_identifier`. Ruling: add these variants, or list which existing variant covers each rule in a doc line.

**F4. "One malformed fixture per `RQuirk`" with `(malformed)` and `stream_failure: true` is wrong for several quirks.** `KeepaliveWithoutSequence` is exempt (R7) and is conforming. `EventErrorName`, `TopLevelError`, `ErrorEventMidItem` are upstream errors (749 D17). `DoneIncomplete`, `FailedWithOpenItem` are truncations (R15). `Bom` and `NoFinalBlankLine` act at the SSE layer or at EOF and cannot follow a first `added`. Ruling: T9 gets an expected-outcome column per quirk (malformed, upstream error, truncation, conforming); move the exempt ones to the conforming set.

**F5. Golden fixture names are not in the conforming list.** T9 Step 1 gives conforming names "exactly" (`function_blocked`, `reasoning_then_function`, ...). Step 4 uses `function_blocked_deltas`, `builtin_blocked_added_done`, `truncated_item`, `blocked_after_reasoning`. Ruling: add the four names to Step 1, or map them to existing names.

**F6. A recorded truncated stream cannot "pass unchanged".** T1 records `max_output_tokens_in_call`; T9 `recorded_streams_pass_unchanged` and spec § 10.5 require no deviation and unchanged output under allow-all. A truncated item blocks the hold with `Truncated` whatever the decider says. Ruling: exclude the M5 recording from that test and give it its own expected-rewrite test, or keep it out of `recorded/`.

**F7. Non-stream truncation is a 502/malformed; stream truncation is a rewrite.** Plan decision, T5 (`item_not_completed`), Review Focus 3. Spec § 6.5 non-stream says "same replacement" and "749 § 4.4", and is silent on `status`. Ruling: accept, and add one line to spec § 6.5 so spec and code agree (AC 9: "the spec agrees").

**F8. Second terminal event: deviation or silent drop?** T4 `second_terminal` is a `Deviation`; R3 and T6 drop any record after the terminal (`AfterEnd`). Through the stream, `AfterEnd` fires first, so `second_terminal` cannot occur. Ruling: drop the `second_terminal` deviation, or state that `AfterEnd` is checked after `accept`.

**F9. Oracle model kinds collapse to `item`.** Spec § 10.1: "Each new kind gets its own model kind." T7 `responses_kind_of` maps every other kind to `item`; the name is then the only discriminator (and for `Other` the name is the item type). Ruling: accept, with a doc line, or add the six kinds.

**F10. `capture.py` changes are under-specified.** Make `--key-file` optional under `--dry-run`; allow the new scenario names in `--only` (today `choices=sorted(SCENARIOS)`); state the dry-run file count (15 only if two-request scenarios write one file each; M6 has three variants).

**F11. Number check is wider than the spec.** Spec § 7.1: `check_numbers` runs on the envelope and on each client-run item only. T3 `check_numbers_responses` checks everything outside data subtrees (provider-run and message items too). A lossy number in a provider item would then fail a stream the spec lets through. Ruling: restrict to the envelope and client-run items.

**F12. Mutation step may die at rustc.** T8 Step 4 removes the R5 check. Under `-D warnings` an unused binding stops the build before any property runs, and R4/R6 may catch the interleave first. Ruling: say "the mutation must compile; use `--no-fail-fast`" and name a quirk that only R5 catches.

**F13. Review Focus 5 is only half pinned.** T13 tests 70 KiB and 2 MiB, not above 16 MiB. T14 asserts the charge only for the over-16 MiB case, not the D13 or `(malformed)` client side. Ruling: add a scanner test above 16 MiB and an HTTP assertion for the client bytes.

**F14. Commit trailer.** Global Constraints mandate `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`. The session attribution reminder names Sonnet 5.5. Ruling: coordinator picks one; the plan text should not hard-code a model.

**F15. Small wording defects.** T2: `report_entry` is "private" and also moved to `report.rs` as `pub(crate)`. Global Constraints: one `#![cfg_attr(...)]` "on `turn::responses`" cannot be an inner attribute on a function; use `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`.

**F16. T11 says the router mounts the route; it has no handler.** Interfaces: "The router mounts `POST /v1/responses` only when `state.responses` is `Some`" and "Task 14 ... mounts the route." Ruling: T11 adds no route; T14 mounts it.

## Findings

**F1. Global Constraints forbid edits the tasks require.** Plan: "The only edit allowed in an existing test file is `responses: None` ... and new test functions." Tasks that edit existing test files otherwise: T7 (`ModelCall` fields in `tests/support/oracle.rs`), T8 (`streams.rs`), T9 (`golden.rs` `SET`, `manifest.json`, edits to existing tests in `fixtures.rs`), T10 (`RecordedRequest.path`), T14 (`tests/support/mod.rs` mock), T16 (rename of `test_manifest_lists_six_goldens`). Spec AC 8 says only that the existing tests pass. Ruling: reword the constraint: "existing tests keep their assertions; helper types and sets may grow".

**F2. The oracle reads calls from `added` for built-in kinds, but R13 lets `shell_call` `added` differ from `done`.** Plan T7 / spec § 10.1: openai-python `ResponseStream` calls come from every `output_item.added` item of kinds other than function and custom. R13: `added` and `done` differ in `action.commands`. An allowed, conforming `shell_call` then gives a model call that differs from the decided call, so P1 can fail on a good stream (T8 generates `shell_call`). Ruling: for `shell_call`, take the model call from `done` only, or require `added.action.commands` to be the decided value. Say which in T7.

**F3. Quirks do not cover every rule.** Spec § 10.3 / AC 4: "every rule of § 6.4 gets a generator quirk." The `RQuirk` list has none for R1 `first_not_created`, R3 `second_terminal`, R4 `index_order`, R6 `wrong_item_index`, R10 `terminal_output_mismatch` (partly), R11 `arguments_mismatch`, R12 `input_mismatch`, R14 `added_done_differ`, `long_identifier`. Ruling: add these variants, or list which existing variant covers each rule in a doc line.

**F4. "One malformed fixture per `RQuirk`" with `(malformed)` and `stream_failure: true` is wrong for several quirks.** `KeepaliveWithoutSequence` is exempt (R7) and is conforming. `EventErrorName`, `TopLevelError`, `ErrorEventMidItem` are upstream errors (749 D17). `DoneIncomplete`, `FailedWithOpenItem` are truncations (R15). `Bom` and `NoFinalBlankLine` act at the SSE layer or at EOF and cannot follow a first `added`. Ruling: T9 gets an expected-outcome column per quirk (malformed, upstream error, truncation, conforming); move the exempt ones to the conforming set.

**F5. Golden fixture names are not in the conforming list.** T9 Step 1 gives conforming names "exactly" (`function_blocked`, `reasoning_then_function`, ...). Step 4 uses `function_blocked_deltas`, `builtin_blocked_added_done`, `truncated_item`, `blocked_after_reasoning`. Ruling: add the four names to Step 1, or map them to existing names.

**F6. A recorded truncated stream cannot "pass unchanged".** T1 records `max_output_tokens_in_call`; T9 `recorded_streams_pass_unchanged` and spec § 10.5 require no deviation and unchanged output under allow-all. A truncated item blocks the hold with `Truncated` whatever the decider says. Ruling: exclude the M5 recording from that test and give it its own expected-rewrite test, or keep it out of `recorded/`.

**F7. Non-stream truncation is a 502/malformed; stream truncation is a rewrite.** Plan decision, T5 (`item_not_completed`), Review Focus 3. Spec § 6.5 non-stream says "same replacement" and "749 § 4.4", and is silent on `status`. Ruling: accept, and add one line to spec § 6.5 so spec and code agree (AC 9: "the spec agrees").

**F8. Second terminal event: deviation or silent drop?** T4 `second_terminal` is a `Deviation`; R3 and T6 drop any record after the terminal (`AfterEnd`). Through the stream, `AfterEnd` fires first, so `second_terminal` cannot occur. Ruling: drop the `second_terminal` deviation, or state that `AfterEnd` is checked after `accept`.

**F9. Oracle model kinds collapse to `item`.** Spec § 10.1: "Each new kind gets its own model kind." T7 `responses_kind_of` maps every other kind to `item`; the name is then the only discriminator (and for `Other` the name is the item type). Ruling: accept, with a doc line, or add the six kinds.

**F10. `capture.py` changes are under-specified.** Make `--key-file` optional under `--dry-run`; allow the new scenario names in `--only` (today `choices=sorted(SCENARIOS)`); state the dry-run file count (15 only if two-request scenarios write one file each; M6 has three variants).

**F11. Number check is wider than the spec.** Spec § 7.1: `check_numbers` runs on the envelope and on each client-run item only. T3 `check_numbers_responses` checks everything outside data subtrees (provider-run and message items too). A lossy number in a provider item would then fail a stream the spec lets through. Ruling: restrict to the envelope and client-run items.

**F12. Mutation step may die at rustc.** T8 Step 4 removes the R5 check. Under `-D warnings` an unused binding stops the build before any property runs, and R4/R6 may catch the interleave first. Ruling: say "the mutation must compile; use `--no-fail-fast`" and name a quirk that only R5 catches.

**F13. Review Focus 5 is only half pinned.** T13 tests 70 KiB and 2 MiB, not above 16 MiB. T14 asserts the charge only for the over-16 MiB case, not the D13 or `(malformed)` client side. Ruling: add a scanner test above 16 MiB and an HTTP assertion for the client bytes.

**F14. Commit trailer.** Global Constraints mandate `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`. The session attribution reminder names Sonnet 5.5. Ruling: coordinator picks one; the plan text should not hard-code a model.

**F15. Small wording defects.** T2: `report_entry` is "private" and also moved to `report.rs` as `pub(crate)`. Global Constraints: one `#![cfg_attr(...)]` "on `turn::responses`" cannot be an inner attribute on a function; use `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`.

**F16. T11 says the router mounts the route; it has no handler.** Interfaces: "The router mounts `POST /v1/responses` only when `state.responses` is `Some`" and "Task 14 ... mounts the route." Ruling: T11 adds no route; T14 mounts it.

## 4. Decisions

| Id | Question | Decision |
|----|----------|----------|
| D1 | Where the format lives | A new module `paigasus-gateway-core::responses` (`classify`, `assembly`, `stream`, `body`), with its own `Protocol` implementation. It shares only the generic parts: `json`, `sse`, `report`, `interceptor`, `body`, `turn`. `ChoiceAssembly` does not change. |
| D2 | New core types | `Format::OpenAiResponses`. `HoldKey::Response` (one hold per response, D10). New `ToolCallKind` variants: `Computer`, `LocalShell`, `Shell`, `ApplyPatch`, `ToolSearch`, `McpApprovalRequest`. `function_call` uses `Function`, `custom_tool_call` uses `Custom`. `ToolCall` gets `namespace: Option<String>`. |
| D3 | Server-side state | **Stateless only.** With interception enabled (the global `[tool_interception] enabled`, that is `AppState.tool_interception` is `Some`, known before admission), a request is refused with 400 `responses-stateful-not-supported` when it has a non-null `previous_response_id`, `conversation` or `prompt`, or an `item_reference` input item. |
| D4 | Background mode | `background: true` is refused with the same 400, whether interception is enabled or not. The gateway has no route for `GET /v1/responses/{id}`, so a background result cannot be fetched through it. |
| D5 | `store` | The request body is forwarded unchanged. The gateway does not set `store: false`. D3 already stops every later turn from reading the stored output. A rewrite of `store` would be the first request rewrite (749 non-goal). Operator note: with `store` true, OpenAI keeps the output, including a blocked call, for its retention period (§ 9). |
| D6 | Service shape | One generic handler pipeline with an endpoint descriptor per route (§ 8). `/v1/chat/completions` moves to it with no change in behaviour. The descriptor is for OpenAI-shaped routes. SMA-750 decides whether it extends it. |
| D7 | Upstream | `OpenAiClient` gets one method that takes a closed `UpstreamRoute` enum (`ChatCompletions`, `Responses`), never a free path. `Responses` forwards to `{base_url}/v1/responses` with the same headers, timeouts and cancellation as chat. |
| D8 | Route switch | A new `[responses] enabled` config key, default `false`. When it is `false`, `/v1/responses` returns 404. Rollback is this key, with no deploy. |
| D9 | Streaming switch | Streaming obeys the existing `stream_enabled`. No new capability is advertised (749 D28). |
| D10 | The hold | **One hold per response.** It opens at the first client-run item's `added` frame and completes at the terminal event. The decider gets every client-run call of the response in one `decide` call, as it gets every call of choice 0 in chat. A truncation (§ 6.4, R15) blocks every call of the hold with `Truncated`. |
| D11 | Output framing | Re-framed as in 749 D3, with an `event: <data.type>` line before each `data:` line. `unframed()` uses the same form. `[DONE]` has no `event:` line. |
| D12 | Rewrite | A blocked item becomes a `message` item at the same `output_index`, frame by frame (§ 6.5). No other index changes. |

### Reasons

- **D1.** Responses streams are item-based: each event has an `output_index` and an `item_id`, and
  `*.done` events repeat the full value. Chat Completions streams index-delta fragments. A shared
  assembly would put Responses cases into the code path that SMA-757 proved.
- **D3.** The gateway cannot see a turn that OpenAI stores. A decision then has no `prior_calls` or
  `tool_results`, and SMA-753 sequence rules fail open. A blocked call also stays in OpenAI's
  stored output, which the client never saw (M1). A `prompt` template can add tools that the
  gateway cannot see. With interception off, the gateway is a plain proxy, and these fields do no
  harm through it.
- **D8.** Billing and availability depend on shapes that are first measured in this change (M2,
  M7). An operator must be able to turn the route off without a deploy.
- **D10.** SMA-752 and SMA-753 policies that limit the calls per turn need every call of the turn
  in one decision. Chat gives them that per choice. A hold per item would give them one call at a
  time. The cost: frames after the first client-run item wait until the terminal event. Chat has
  the same cost until `finish_reason`.

  renumbering, which is the main cost of the chat rewrite.

  event over 1 MiB would fail the stream, and every SDK raises without `response.created` or a

  call. A report of "unenforceable" would let a client run an action that was never decided.

### 6.2 Item classes

- **Tool-free content:** `message`, `reasoning`, `compaction`.
- **Provider-run, reported `unenforceable`, never decided:** `web_search_call`, `file_search_call`,
  `code_interpreter_call`, `image_generation_call`, `mcp_call`, `mcp_list_tools`, `program`,
  `program_output`, `additional_tools`, `tool_search_output`, `shell_call_output`,
  `local_shell_call_output`, `computer_call_output`, `apply_patch_call_output`. This is the
  treatment of Anthropic `server_tool_use` (749 § 4.2): the item opens no hold, its frames are
  forwarded in stream order (behind an open hold, 749 D12), and one report entry with
  `decision: "unenforceable"` is emitted. `on_failure` never applies to it.
- **Client-run (held and decided):** `function_call` (Function), `custom_tool_call` (Custom),
  `computer_call` (Computer), `local_shell_call` (LocalShell), `shell_call` (Shell),
  `apply_patch_call` (ApplyPatch), `tool_search_call` (ToolSearch), `mcp_approval_request`
  (McpApprovalRequest).
- **Any other item type**, including `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output` and
  `mcp_approval_response` in the output: client-run, kind `Other` (fail closed).

`shell_call` and `tool_search_call` are client-run for every value of `environment` and
`execution`. The class must be fixed at `added`, and these fields can be absent there. A hosted
shell or a server search then runs on the provider even when the decision is `block`. The report
says `block` for it, and the notice replaces it for the client. This is a known limit: the
SMA-755 log must not treat such a block as a prevented action (spec author's call).

A `function_call` with a `caller` of type `program` is still a client-run `function_call`.

### 6.3 Record classification

Dispatch on `data.type`. A present `event:` name that differs from `data.type` is malformed. A
record with a top-level `error` key whose value is truthy, and a `type: "error"` record, are
upstream error records (749 D17 when a hold is open; forwarded otherwise). `[DONE]` ends the
stream. The known types are the 59 members of openai-python 3.48.0's `ResponseStreamEvent` union
plus `keepalive`, plus the two `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.*` types (A4). Any other
type is malformed. openai-node 7.57.0 does not know the two diff types and raises at the first one
(`Unhandled response stream event`), on upstream bytes too. So a Node client cannot stream an
`apply_patch_call` with or without the gateway.

### 6.4 Canonical rules (any deviation: stream-level `on_failure`, code `Malformed`)

`keepalive` and the upstream error record are exempt from R1, R2 and R7.

Stream order:

- R1. The first record is `response.created`. Every lifecycle event has the same `response.id`.
  A `response.created` after the first record is a deviation (`repeated_created`).
- R2. `response.created`, `response.queued` and `response.in_progress` carry `response.output: []`.
- R3. Exactly one terminal event (`response.completed`, `response.incomplete` or
  `response.failed`). It carries `response.output` as an array, never absent or `null` (R-d).
  After it, only `[DONE]` may follow; `[DONE]` is then emitted. Any other record after it is
  dropped and counted (749 D4).
- R4. `output_index` values first appear in order 0, 1, 2, …, each on one
  `response.output_item.added`. Each index has exactly one `added` and at most one `done`.
- R5. The events of an item are contiguous: no event of another item arrives between its `added`
  and its `done` (M3).
- R6. Every item-scoped event has the `output_index` of the open item, and its `item_id` (where
  the type has one) equals that item's `id`. The event type matches the item type (§ 6.1).
- R7. `sequence_number`, when present, is an integer that strictly increases. Either every event
  has it or none does.
- R8. `added.item` is an object with a string `type` and a non-empty string `id`. Item `id`s are
  unique in the response, and `call_id`s are unique in the response. No upstream `id` starts with
  `msg_paigasus_`.

Every item, of every class (R-b):

- R9. `type`, `id`, `call_id`, `namespace` and `name` (each where the type has it) are equal in
  `added`, `done` and the item at the same index in the terminal `output`.
- R10. The terminal `output` has exactly one item per streamed `output_index`, in order, and no
  other item. A **client-run** item with a `done` frame equals its `done` item as a JSON value in
  the terminal `output`. A tool-free or provider-run item needs only R9 there: the measured
  `reasoning` items have a different `encrypted_content` in the terminal `output` (§ 3.3,
  amendment A1).

Per client-run item (R-a, R-e). The decided value is always the `done` item (§ 5). The **subset
rule**: every field of the `added` item, at any depth, except `status`, is absent, `null`, `""`,
`[]`, or equal to the same field of the `done` item; and the `added` item has no field that the
`done` item does not have (amendment A2, measured § 3.3):

- R11. `function_call`: `added.item.arguments` is `""`. The concatenated
  `function_call_arguments.delta` values equal `function_call_arguments.done.arguments`, which
  equals `done.item.arguments`. When the `done` status is `"completed"`, the arguments are `""`
  or one complete JSON value (749 § 11 `incomplete_arguments`). Any other `done` status is R15,
  and R15 takes precedence (amendment A3).
- R12. `custom_tool_call`: the same rule with `input` and `custom_tool_call_input.*`. `input` is
  free text.
- R13. `shell_call`: per command index i, the `shell_call_command.added` command plus its deltas
  equal its `shell_call_command.done` command, which equals `done.item.action.commands[i]`.
  Indexes appear in order. The subset rule applies to every other field (for example
  `action.max_output_length`: `null` at `added`, `20000` at `done`). `added.item.action.commands`
  is `[]` or equals the `done` commands (preflight ruling F2).
- R14. `apply_patch_call`: the concatenated `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta` values
  equal `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.done.diff`, which equals
  `done.item.operation.diff`. The subset rule applies to every other field. The other client-run
  kinds (`computer_call`, `local_shell_call`, `tool_search_call`, `mcp_approval_request`): the
  subset rule (for example `computer_call` `actions`: absent at `added`, present at `done`).
- R15. A client-run item whose `done` has a `status` other than `"completed"` is a truncation (M5).
  So are a terminal event, `[DONE]` or EOF while a client-run item has no `done`.
- R16. No event for an item arrives after its `done`.

If a measurement (§ 3.3) shows that real traffic breaks a rule, the work stops and the spec
changes first. A rule is not loosened in code.

### 6.5 Rewrite

Only frames that contain a blocked item are re-serialized. A blocked item's frames are rewritten
one by one, so the rule works for a blocked hold, a truncated item, a hold limit and a stream that
fails while the item assembles (`Mode::Failed`):

- The item's `added` frame becomes three events: `response.output_item.added` with the message
  item, `response.content_part.added` with an empty `output_text` part, and
  `response.output_text.delta` with the notice (§ 6.6).
- Every middle frame of the item is dropped.
- The item's `done` frame becomes `response.output_item.done` with the completed message. When the
  item has no `done` frame, this event is synthesized before the next frame of the stream (the
  terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D13 frame), as chat's `closing()` does.
- In the terminal event, the item at a blocked index is always replaced with the completed message.
  This replacement is exempt from R10.

The exact JSON, with `<i>` the blocked `output_index`, `<n>` the notice, and `<s>` the
`sequence_number` of the replaced frame (the key is left out when R7 says none):

```json
{"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"in_progress","content":[]}}
{"type":"response.content_part.added","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "part":{"type":"output_text","text":"","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}}
{"type":"response.output_text.delta","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "delta":"<n>","logprobs":[]}
{"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"completed",
         "content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"<n>","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}]}}
```

The three events from one `added` frame repeat its `sequence_number`. The emitted numbers then do
not strictly increase. No SDK of § 3.2 reads `sequence_number` on a `create` stream (spec author's
call; the Python conformance test of § 10.2 confirms it for openai-python).

No other field of the terminal event changes: `status`, `usage`, `incomplete_details` and `error`
stay as the upstream sent them. If M2 shows a wire `output_text` field, the builder adds the
notice to it and records this here. The Responses API has no `finish_reason`, so nothing else is
rewritten.

**Non-stream.** The same replacement in the body's `output[]` (the completed message). 749 § 4.4
applies otherwise: one re-serialization, and the original bytes when nothing is blocked. A
client-run item with a `status` other than `"completed"` is blocked with code `Truncated` and
replaced, as in the stream (R15; preflight ruling F7).

### 6.6 Notice, names and report

749 § 4.5 and § 4.6 apply. The notice is `[paigasus] tool call "<name>" was blocked (<code>).`.
`<name>` is `ToolCall.name`, prefixed with `<namespace>.` when a namespace is present, then
sanitized. In a report, `choice` is `0` and `position` is the `output_index`.

decided value as the `done` item and keeps every call surface equal to it.

- A1. R10 full equality applies to client-run items only. `reasoning` `encrypted_content`

- **Provider-run, reported `unenforceable`, never decided:** `web_search_call`, `file_search_call`,
  `code_interpreter_call`, `image_generation_call`, `mcp_call`, `mcp_list_tools`, `program`,
  `program_output`, `additional_tools`, `tool_search_output`, `shell_call_output`,
  `local_shell_call_output`, `computer_call_output`, `apply_patch_call_output`. This is the
  treatment of Anthropic `server_tool_use` (749 § 4.2): the item opens no hold, its frames are
  forwarded in stream order (behind an open hold, 749 D12), and one report entry with
  `decision: "unenforceable"` is emitted. `on_failure` never applies to it.
- **Client-run (held and decided):** `function_call` (Function), `custom_tool_call` (Custom),
  `computer_call` (Computer), `local_shell_call` (LocalShell), `shell_call` (Shell),
  `apply_patch_call` (ApplyPatch), `tool_search_call` (ToolSearch), `mcp_approval_request`
  (McpApprovalRequest).
- **Any other item type**, including `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output` and
  `mcp_approval_response` in the output: client-run, kind `Other` (fail closed).

`shell_call` and `tool_search_call` are client-run for every value of `environment` and
`execution`. The class must be fixed at `added`, and these fields can be absent there. A hosted
shell or a server search then runs on the provider even when the decision is `block`. The report
says `block` for it, and the notice replaces it for the client. This is a known limit: the
SMA-755 log must not treat such a block as a prevented action (spec author's call).

A `function_call` with a `caller` of type `program` is still a client-run `function_call`.

### 6.3 Record classification

Dispatch on `data.type`. A present `event:` name that differs from `data.type` is malformed. A
record with a top-level `error` key whose value is truthy, and a `type: "error"` record, are
upstream error records (749 D17 when a hold is open; forwarded otherwise). `[DONE]` ends the
stream. The known types are the 59 members of openai-python 3.48.0's `ResponseStreamEvent` union
plus `keepalive`, plus the two `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.*` types (A4). Any other
type is malformed. openai-node 7.57.0 does not know the two diff types and raises at the first one
(`Unhandled response stream event`), on upstream bytes too. So a Node client cannot stream an
`apply_patch_call` with or without the gateway.

### 6.4 Canonical rules (any deviation: stream-level `on_failure`, code `Malformed`)

`keepalive` and the upstream error record are exempt from R1, R2 and R7.

Stream order:

- R1. The first record is `response.created`. Every lifecycle event has the same `response.id`.
  A `response.created` after the first record is a deviation (`repeated_created`).
- R2. `response.created`, `response.queued` and `response.in_progress` carry `response.output: []`.
- R3. Exactly one terminal event (`response.completed`, `response.incomplete` or
  `response.failed`). It carries `response.output` as an array, never absent or `null` (R-d).
  After it, only `[DONE]` may follow; `[DONE]` is then emitted. Any other record after it is
  dropped and counted (749 D4).
- R4. `output_index` values first appear in order 0, 1, 2, …, each on one
  `response.output_item.added`. Each index has exactly one `added` and at most one `done`.
- R5. The events of an item are contiguous: no event of another item arrives between its `added`
  and its `done` (M3).
- R6. Every item-scoped event has the `output_index` of the open item, and its `item_id` (where
  the type has one) equals that item's `id`. The event type matches the item type (§ 6.1).
- R7. `sequence_number`, when present, is an integer that strictly increases. Either every event
  has it or none does.
- R8. `added.item` is an object with a string `type` and a non-empty string `id`. Item `id`s are
  unique in the response, and `call_id`s are unique in the response. No upstream `id` starts with
  `msg_paigasus_`.

Every item, of every class (R-b):

- R9. `type`, `id`, `call_id`, `namespace` and `name` (each where the type has it) are equal in
  `added`, `done` and the item at the same index in the terminal `output`.
- R10. The terminal `output` has exactly one item per streamed `output_index`, in order, and no
  other item. A **client-run** item with a `done` frame equals its `done` item as a JSON value in
  the terminal `output`. A tool-free or provider-run item needs only R9 there: the measured
  `reasoning` items have a different `encrypted_content` in the terminal `output` (§ 3.3,
  amendment A1).

Per client-run item (R-a, R-e). The decided value is always the `done` item (§ 5). The **subset
rule**: every field of the `added` item, at any depth, except `status`, is absent, `null`, `""`,
`[]`, or equal to the same field of the `done` item; and the `added` item has no field that the
`done` item does not have (amendment A2, measured § 3.3):

- R11. `function_call`: `added.item.arguments` is `""`. The concatenated
  `function_call_arguments.delta` values equal `function_call_arguments.done.arguments`, which
  equals `done.item.arguments`. When the `done` status is `"completed"`, the arguments are `""`
  or one complete JSON value (749 § 11 `incomplete_arguments`). Any other `done` status is R15,
  and R15 takes precedence (amendment A3).
- R12. `custom_tool_call`: the same rule with `input` and `custom_tool_call_input.*`. `input` is
  free text.
- R13. `shell_call`: per command index i, the `shell_call_command.added` command plus its deltas
  equal its `shell_call_command.done` command, which equals `done.item.action.commands[i]`.
  Indexes appear in order. The subset rule applies to every other field (for example
  `action.max_output_length`: `null` at `added`, `20000` at `done`). `added.item.action.commands`
  is `[]` or equals the `done` commands (preflight ruling F2).
- R14. `apply_patch_call`: the concatenated `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta` values
  equal `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.done.diff`, which equals
  `done.item.operation.diff`. The subset rule applies to every other field. The other client-run
  kinds (`computer_call`, `local_shell_call`, `tool_search_call`, `mcp_approval_request`): the
  subset rule (for example `computer_call` `actions`: absent at `added`, present at `done`).
- R15. A client-run item whose `done` has a `status` other than `"completed"` is a truncation (M5).
  So are a terminal event, `[DONE]` or EOF while a client-run item has no `done`.
- R16. No event for an item arrives after its `done`.

If a measurement (§ 3.3) shows that real traffic breaks a rule, the work stops and the spec
changes first. A rule is not loosened in code.

### 6.5 Rewrite

Only frames that contain a blocked item are re-serialized. A blocked item's frames are rewritten
one by one, so the rule works for a blocked hold, a truncated item, a hold limit and a stream that
fails while the item assembles (`Mode::Failed`):

- The item's `added` frame becomes three events: `response.output_item.added` with the message
  item, `response.content_part.added` with an empty `output_text` part, and
  `response.output_text.delta` with the notice (§ 6.6).
- Every middle frame of the item is dropped.
- The item's `done` frame becomes `response.output_item.done` with the completed message. When the
  item has no `done` frame, this event is synthesized before the next frame of the stream (the
  terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D13 frame), as chat's `closing()` does.
- In the terminal event, the item at a blocked index is always replaced with the completed message.
  This replacement is exempt from R10.

The exact JSON, with `<i>` the blocked `output_index`, `<n>` the notice, and `<s>` the
`sequence_number` of the replaced frame (the key is left out when R7 says none):

```json
{"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"in_progress","content":[]}}
{"type":"response.content_part.added","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "part":{"type":"output_text","text":"","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}}
{"type":"response.output_text.delta","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "delta":"<n>","logprobs":[]}
{"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"completed",
         "content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"<n>","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}]}}
```

The three events from one `added` frame repeat its `sequence_number`. The emitted numbers then do
not strictly increase. No SDK of § 3.2 reads `sequence_number` on a `create` stream (spec author's
call; the Python conformance test of § 10.2 confirms it for openai-python).

No other field of the terminal event changes: `status`, `usage`, `incomplete_details` and `error`
stay as the upstream sent them. If M2 shows a wire `output_text` field, the builder adds the
notice to it and records this here. The Responses API has no `finish_reason`, so nothing else is
rewritten.

**Non-stream.** The same replacement in the body's `output[]` (the completed message). 749 § 4.4
applies otherwise: one re-serialization, and the original bytes when nothing is blocked. A
client-run item with a `status` other than `"completed"` is blocked with code `Truncated` and
replaced, as in the stream (R15; preflight ruling F7).

### 6.6 Notice, names and report

749 § 4.5 and § 4.6 apply. The notice is `[paigasus] tool call "<name>" was blocked (<code>).`.
`<name>` is `ToolCall.name`, prefixed with `<namespace>.` when a namespace is present, then
sanitized. In a report, `choice` is `0` and `position` is the `output_index`.

## 7. Request side and strict JSON
## 15. Amendments after the measurements (2026-11-14, Task 1)

Task 1 measured real traffic (§ 3.3). Four rules did not match it. Each amendment keeps the
decided value as the `done` item and keeps every call surface equal to it.

- A1. R10 full equality applies to client-run items only. `reasoning` `encrypted_content`
  differs between `done` and the terminal `output` in 26 of 26 items. Tool-free and provider-run
  items keep R9.
- A2. The subset rule replaces "`added` equals `done`" for the built-in client-run kinds (R13,
  R14). Measured: `computer_call` `actions` absent at `added`; `apply_patch_call`
  `operation.diff` `""` at `added`; `shell_call` `action.max_output_length` `null` at `added`.
- A3. R15 takes precedence over R11: a `done` with `status: "incomplete"` has partial JSON
  arguments in 9 of 9 cut calls. It is a truncation (block, `Truncated`), not `Malformed`.
- A4. Two event types that the openai-python 3.48.0 union does not have:
  `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta` and `.done`. They are known types now, mapped
  to `apply_patch_call`, with the diff rule in R14.
- A5. The openai-python `ResponseStream` model no longer counts `output_item.added` items as
  calls (§ 10.1). Under A2, an `added` item is a partial view by design.

### 3.3 To measure in the implementation (§ 10.5, the first task)

- M1. A continuation with `previous_response_id` after a function call that the client did not
  answer. Expected: a 400 error. This is a reason for D3. D3 stays whatever the result, because
  the gateway still cannot see the earlier turns.
  Measured 2026-11-14 (the `.measure.json` files of `capture.py`): 3 of 3 models
  (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-4.1`) refused the
  continuation with HTTP 400, type `invalid_request_error`, `param` `"input"`, `code` `null` and
  the message `No tool output found for function call <call_id>.`. The first call was a non-stream
  call with `store: true` and a forced function call.
- M2. Whether OpenAI sends `event:` lines, `[DONE]`, `sequence_number`, `obfuscation`, a wire
  `output_text`, and `keepalive` events on Responses streams, and the position of each.
  Measured 2026-11-14 on 78 streams of the 3 models (§ 10.5), with the committed `measure.py`.
  The fields named here are its output fields. `event_lines`: every record has an `event:` line,
  equal to `data.type` (78 of 78). `done_marker`: no stream has `[DONE]` (0 of 78), so the stream
  ends after the terminal event. `sequence_number`: on every event, `starts_at_zero` and `no_gap`
  (78 of 78). `obfuscation.types` holds only `*.delta` types (6 types in all streams), and
  `on_every_delta` is true in 78 of 78. `obfuscation.present` is true in 77 of 78: the one
  `computer_call` stream has no delta event. `wire_output_text`: no terminal `response` has an
  `output_text` key (0 of 78). So the § 6.5 sentence about a wire `output_text` does not apply.
  `keepalive`: 0 events in 78 of 78.
- M3. Whether the events of one output item are contiguous, and whether `output_index` stays the
  same from `added` to `done` (R-f). Include a stream with several provider-run tool calls.
  Measured 2026-11-14 with `measure.py`: `contiguous` (R5) holds in 78 of 78 streams, and
  `index_stable` holds in 78 of 78. `item_types`: 6 streams have two provider-run
  `web_search_call` items and then a `function_call` (`gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6.1-terra`,
  `web_search_then_function`). `gpt-4.1` did not search in 3 of 3 runs. `rules`: R1 to R4, R6,
  R8, R9 and R16 have no break in 78 of 78. `done_vs_terminal` (R10, per item type): every
  `function_call` (78), `custom_tool_call` (6), `computer_call`, `apply_patch_call`, `shell_call`
  (1 each), `message` (21) and `web_search_call` (12) `done` item equals its terminal `output`
  item. **R10 does not hold for `reasoning` items:** 26 of 26 differ (one in each of 26 streams of
  `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6.1-terra`), and the only key that differs is `encrypted_content`. The
  requests did not ask for `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` (see `capture.py --dry-run`).
- M4. The `added`, delta and `done` shapes of each client-run kind that can be recorded: whether
  `function_call` `added` carries `arguments: ""`, and whether `computer_call`,
  `apply_patch_call`, `shell_call` and `local_shell_call` are complete at `added`.
  Measured 2026-11-14 with `measure.py` (`added_shapes`). `function_call`: `arguments_at_added`
  is `""` and `deltas_equal_done` is true for 78 items in 51 streams. `custom_tool_call`:
  `input_at_added` is `""` and `deltas_equal_done` is true for 6 items in the 6 `custom_forced`
  streams of `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6.1-terra`. No model made a custom call and a function call in
  one response (`custom_and_function`: 6 of 6 runs made only function calls). `gpt-4.1` refuses
  `custom` tools: HTTP 400, `Invalid value: 'custom'`, code `unknown_parameter` (6 of 6
  `.error.json` files of `capture.py`). The built-in kinds were recorded once each on
  `gpt-6.1-sol`:
  `computer_call` is **not** complete at `added`: `differs_from_done` is
  `["actions (only at done)"]`. The stream has no event type other than the lifecycle events and
  `output_item.added`/`.done` (`max_record_bytes` keys). This breaks R14.
  `apply_patch_call` is **not** complete at `added`: `differs_from_done` is `["operation.diff"]`.
  The diff streams in `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta` events and a `.done`
  event, and `diff_deltas_equal_done` is true. These events carry `item_id`
  (`events_without_item_id` does not list them). This breaks R14. A grep of the openai-python
  3.48.0 sources finds neither event type, so they are not in its `ResponseStreamEvent` union and
  not in the § 6.1 map. Then § 6.3 makes them malformed.
  `shell_call`: `commands_at_added` is `[]`, and `commands_from_events_equal_done` is true (the
  `shell_call_command.added` command plus its deltas equals the `.done` command and
  `done.item.action.commands`). `events_without_item_id` lists the three
  `response.shell_call_command.*` types. `differs_from_done` is
  `["action.commands", "action.max_output_length"]`: `max_output_length` is `null` at `added` and
  `20000` at `done`. This breaks R13.

  supported.` (`param` `"tools"`). `tool_search_call` and `mcp_approval_request` were not tried.

  `status: "incomplete"`, or no `done`.
  Measured 2026-11-14 with `measure.py` in 9 of 9 cut streams (3 per model,
  `max_output_tokens: 48`): `terminal` is `response.incomplete`, and `done_status` of the
  `function_call` is `"incomplete"`, so OpenAI sends the `done`. `deltas_equal_done` is true, so a
  `function_call_arguments.done` event has the same arguments as the deltas and the `done` item.
  `arguments_complete_json` is false (9 of 9). So R15 sees a truncation. R11 also applies to the
  same item ("`""` or one complete JSON value"), and this spec does not say which rule wins.
- M6. A next turn after a rewrite: replay a rewritten output (a `reasoning` item followed by the
  `msg_paigasus_…` message) as `input`, with and without `store`, with
  `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. Expected unknown. If OpenAI rejects it, the rewrite
  (§ 6.5) changes before implementation.
  Measured 2026-11-14 (the `.measure.json` files of `capture.py`): OpenAI accepted the rewritten
  output in 9 of 9 requests (3 models,
  3 variants each, HTTP 200, `status: "completed"`). Only `gpt-6.1-sol` put a `reasoning` item
  before the call. Its replay was `reasoning`, then `msg_paigasus_1`, then a user message, in all
  3 variants. `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-4.1` made only a `function_call`, so their replay had
  `msg_paigasus_0` and no `reasoning` item. Limit: the one first call per model used
  `store: true` and `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. So the `store: false` variant
  replayed a `reasoning` item that had `encrypted_content`. A `reasoning` item without
  `encrypted_content` with `store: false` was not measured.
- M7. The byte size of `response.created` and `response.completed` with a long `instructions`
  (about 50 KB) and 30 tool schemas.
  Measured 2026-11-14 with `measure.py` (`max_record_bytes`, the whole record with the `event:`
  line) in 9 streams of `long_instructions_30_tools` (50,000 bytes of `instructions`, 30 function
  tools): `response.created` is 60,472 to 60,507 bytes, `response.in_progress` is 60,480 to
  60,515 bytes, and `response.completed` is 60,933 to 60,976 bytes. In the 78 streams, the largest
  record of any other type is 4,885 bytes (`response.incomplete`). Outside the 9 long streams,
  the largest record is 6,175 bytes (`response.completed`). All are below 64 KiB and far below the
  D15 limits.

## 7. Request side and strict JSON

### 7.1 Strict JSON per format

- The Responses data subtrees are: `tools[]` (whole entries), `text`, `metadata`, `instructions`,
  `prompt`, `reasoning`, and `input` (request); `response.tools`, `response.text`,
  `response.metadata`, `response.instructions`, `response.prompt` and `response.reasoning`
  (lifecycle events and the non-stream body). Below a data subtree, the `parse_value_strict` rules
  apply.
- `check_numbers` runs on the envelope and on each client-run item only, not on data subtrees.
- The Responses classifier keys (`type`, `output_index`, `item_id`, `call_id`, `item`, `output`,
  `arguments`, `input`, `name`, `namespace`, `id`, `delta`, `response`, `error`) are a per-format
  list. The chat and Anthropic lists do not change.
- A test shows that a structured-output schema with properties `Name`, `ID`, `Type` and
  `constructor`, a metadata key `Id` and a schema `maximum: 1e300` pass unchanged on stream and
  body.

### 7.2 `TurnFacts`

- The handler parses a copy of the body into a `ResponsesRequest` DTO: `model`, `input`, `stream`,
  `background`, `previous_response_id`, `conversation`, `prompt`, all `Option`, and the rest as
  `extra`. `input` is a string or an array. A body that is not a JSON object is a 400, as in chat.
- D3 and D4 are checked before `Limits::admit`, so a refused request is not counted or charged.
- `definitions` from `tools[]`: function and custom names (with `namespace` from `namespace`
  tools), and the built-in tool types.
- `prior_calls` from the client-run item types of § 6.2 in `input`. `tool_results` from
  `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output`, `computer_call_output`,
  `local_shell_call_output`, `shell_call_output`, `apply_patch_call_output` and
  `mcp_approval_response`.
- `TurnFacts` gets a `definitions_complete: bool`. It is `false` when `tools[]` has a `tool_search`
  tool, or when `input` has an `additional_tools` or `tool_search_output` item: tools can then be
  added at run time. SMA-752 decides how a policy treats an incomplete set. The chat and Anthropic
  formats set it to `true`.

pub const MODELS: &[(&str, Model)] = &[
    ("openai-python", openai_python),
    ("openai-node", openai_node),
    ("langchain", langchain),
    ("anthropic-python", anthropic_python),
];

const OPENAI_RUNNERS: &[(&str, Runner)] = &[("openai-python", run_openai_python), ("openai-node", run_openai_node), ("langchain", run_langchain)];
const ANTHROPIC_RUNNERS: &[(&str, Runner)] = &[("anthropic-python", run_anthropic_python)];

/// The models of the clients that read `format`.
pub fn runners(format: Format) -> &'static [(&'static str, Runner)] {
    match format {
        Format::AnthropicMessages => ANTHROPIC_RUNNERS,
        _ => OPENAI_RUNNERS,
    }
}

/// The model kind of a decided call.
pub fn kind_of(k: ToolCallKind) -> &'static str {
    match k {
        ToolCallKind::Function => "function",
        ToolCallKind::Custom => "custom",
        ToolCallKind::LegacyFunctionCall => "legacy",
        ToolCallKind::AnthropicToolUse => "tool_use",
        _ => "other",
# Recorded OpenAI Responses streams

These files are live recordings of OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) streams. They were
recorded on 2026-11-14 for SMA-769 (spec § 3.3, § 10.5). They are not hand-built. Each file holds
the raw response bytes, unchanged.

- Models: `gpt-6.1-sol` (no reasoning-effort override), `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-4.1`.
- Scenarios, 3 runs per model: `parallel_functions`, `custom_and_function`, `custom_forced`,
  `reasoning_then_call`, `text_only`, `structured_output`, `web_search_then_function`,
  `max_output_tokens_in_call` and `long_instructions_30_tools`.
- Scenarios, 1 run on `gpt-6.1-sol` only: `apply_patch_forced`, `shell_forced`,
  `local_shell_forced` and `computer_forced`.
- Continuations, 1 run per model: `m1_unanswered_continuation` and `m6_rewrite_replay`. They
  write `.measure.json` files, not streams, so this directory keeps none of them.

The run made 78 streams. This directory keeps 17 of them: the first run of each model and
scenario that obeyed every rule of spec § 6.4 as it was before the § 15 amendments. The check
used `../../openai/recorded/measure.py`. A file is named `<model>__<scenario>.sse`.

No test replays this directory yet. Task 9 adds the replay. The `recorded_streams_pass_unchanged`
test in `tests/fixtures.rs` reads only `openai/recorded/`, as Chat Completions streams. The three
`max_output_tokens_in_call` files end with a `function_call` that has `status: "incomplete"`.
The replay must expect a `Truncated` block for that call (spec § 15, A3), not a pass with no
change.

## What was rejected

- `gpt-4.1` refuses `custom` tools: HTTP 400, `Invalid value: 'custom'`, code
  `unknown_parameter`. So `gpt-4.1` has no `custom_and_function` and no `custom_forced` file.
- `gpt-6.1-sol` refuses the `local_shell` tool: HTTP 400, `The local_shell tool is no longer
  supported.`. So no file has a `local_shell_call`.

## What was recorded but not kept

These streams broke a rule of spec § 6.4 as it was on the day of the run. They are not in this
directory. The spec § 15 amendments A1, A2 and A4 changed those rules after the run. This
directory does not add the streams again.

- Every stream with a `reasoning` item (26 streams of `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6.1-terra`) breaks
  R10. The `encrypted_content` of the `reasoning` item in the terminal `output` is different from
  the one in `response.output_item.done`. So `gpt-6.1-sol` has no `reasoning_then_call`,
  `text_only`, `structured_output` and `max_output_tokens_in_call` file, and `gpt-6.1-terra` has
  no `custom_and_function`, `reasoning_then_call`, `structured_output` and
  `web_search_then_function` file.
- `gpt-6.1-sol__computer_forced`: `added` has no `actions`, and `done` has them. This breaks R14.
- `gpt-6.1-sol__apply_patch_forced`: `added` has `operation.diff: ""`, and the diff streams in
  `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta` and `.done` events. This breaks R14, and these
  event types are not in the § 6.1 map.
- `gpt-6.1-sol__shell_forced`: `action.max_output_length` is `null` at `added` and `20000` at
  `done`. This breaks R13.

## Client-run kinds with no recording here

Task 9 builds these from the openai-python 3.48.0 types: `computer_call`, `apply_patch_call`,
`shell_call`, `local_shell_call`, `tool_search_call` and `mcp_approval_request`. No model made a
`custom_tool_call` and a `function_call` in one response.

## The M1 to M7 results

The full results with the counts are in spec § 3.3.

- M1. A `previous_response_id` continuation with no `function_call_output` gets HTTP 400,
  `No tool output found for function call <call_id>.` (3 of 3 models).
- M2. Every record has an `event:` line equal to `data.type`. No stream has `[DONE]`. Every
  event has `sequence_number`, from 0 and with no gap. Every `*.delta` event has `obfuscation`, and no other event type has it.
  No terminal `response` has `output_text`. No stream has a `keepalive` event.
- M3. The events of each item are contiguous, and `output_index` does not change from `added` to
  `done` (78 of 78). R10 does not hold for `reasoning` items (see above).
- M4. `function_call` and `custom_tool_call` start with `""` at `added`. `computer_call`,
  `apply_patch_call` and `shell_call` are not complete at `added` (see above).
- M5. A cut function call gets `output_item.done` with `status: "incomplete"` and arguments that
  are not complete JSON, then `response.incomplete` (9 of 9).
- M6. OpenAI accepts the § 6.5 rewritten output as `input` with `store: true`, with
  `store: false`, and with `store: false` and `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` (9 of 9).
- M7. With 50,000 bytes of `instructions` and 30 tools, `response.created` is at most 60,507
  bytes and `response.completed` is at most 60,976 bytes.

## Record again

`capture.py` and `measure.py` are in `../../openai/recorded/`. They use only the Python standard
library. Keep the API key in a file outside the repository. The script reads the key from that
file and never prints it.

    python3 -I capture.py --api responses --dry-run --model gpt-6.1-sol --runs 1 --out <dir>
    python3 -I capture.py --api responses --key-file ~/.config/paigasus/openai.key \
        --model <id> --runs 3 --out <dir> --only parallel_functions custom_and_function \
        custom_forced reasoning_then_call text_only structured_output web_search_then_function \
        max_output_tokens_in_call long_instructions_30_tools
    python3 -I capture.py --api responses --key-file ~/.config/paigasus/openai.key \
        --model gpt-6.1-sol --runs 1 --out <dir> --only apply_patch_forced shell_forced \
        local_shell_forced computer_forced
    python3 -I capture.py --api responses --key-file ~/.config/paigasus/openai.key \
        --model <id> --runs 1 --out <dir> --only m1_unanswered_continuation m6_rewrite_replay
    python3 -I measure.py <dir>
