# Task 6 report: the Responses stream protocol, and the format goes live

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. Commit `da4bb7ae feat(rs): intercept responses streams with one hold per response (SMA-769)`.

## What I implemented

- `src/responses/stream.rs` (new): `ResponsesStream::with_cap(cap)`, `impl Protocol`.
  - `step`: R3 check first (after the terminal event, every record except `[DONE]` is `StepError::AfterEnd`, a malformed one too). Then `classify`. `[DONE]` gives `Step::End`. An error record gives `Step::UpstreamError`. A `Known` event goes to `Assembly::accept`. A terminal event gives `Step::Terminal`. Its `completed` list is `[(HoldKey::Response, hold_calls())]` only when the hold is open and not cut.
  - Touches: every frame of a client-run item touches `HoldKey::Response`. The terminal frame touches it only when the hold has opened. Without that condition, a response with no tool call waited for ever (the first test run showed it).
  - `release`: a frame with no blocked item keeps its payload bytes. It gets an `event: <data.type>` line (D11), and `[DONE]` gets none. A blocked item follows § 6.5: `added` gives the three events, middle frames are dropped, `done` gives the completed message. The terminal event gets the completed message at each blocked index. The notice for slot `s` is `notice_line(<qualified name>, code)`, and the names come from `Assembly::known()` (`display_name()`).
  - The synthesized `output_item.done` is written before the terminal frame, `[DONE]`, an error record, EOF (`closing`) and the D13 frame (`closing_on_abort`). Only an item whose rewritten `added` went out can owe one. A keepalive or a `response.audio.*` frame does not end the item. A later real `done` of an item that is already closed is dropped. The synthesized event repeats the `sequence_number` of the item's `added` frame, because no frame is replaced (see Concern 2).
  - `unframed`: writes an `event:` line only when `data.type` matches `^[a-z0-9_.]{1,64}$`.
  - `known_calls(Response)` gives `Assembly::known()`, with the qualified `<namespace>.<name>` names (the carry from Task 2).
- `protocol.rs`: `Step::Terminal { frame, completed }`, `StepError::AfterEnd`, and `Protocol::closing_on_abort` with a default body that returns `Vec::new()`.
- `interceptor.rs`:
  - `Format::OpenAiResponses` uses `ResponsesStream::with_cap(limits.max_held_bytes)`.
  - `Step::Terminal` completes the listed holds, then truncates `incomplete()`, then enqueues the frame.
  - `AfterEnd` counts `RecordDropped("after_done")`.
  - `abort` emits `closing_on_abort` before the terminal frame.
  - A new `after_terminal` flag makes an oversized record after the terminal event `after_done`, not a stream failure (the D4 hazard, applied to R3).
- `responses/assembly.rs`: the end-of-stream entry (the carry from Task 4). `ended()` reports that the terminal event arrived. `hold_cut()` holds the end rule: the hold opened and no terminal event completed it (R3, and R15 with an open item), or a truncation (R15), or an overflow (T4d). The stream decides only a hold that is not cut. A cut hold goes to `incomplete()`, and the interceptor applies `on_failure` to it, never allow. `sequence_numbers()` is now `#[cfg(test)]`, because only tests read it.
- `types.rs`: `Format::OpenAiResponses`.
- `body.rs`: `parse_body(OpenAiResponses)` uses `parse_strict_responses(.., Body)`, `check_numbers_responses(.., Body)`, `responses::body::calls`, and stores `responses::body::forced`. `BodyCalls::code` applies the forced code first, so a forced `Truncated` wins over the decider in `apply` and in `report` (F7). Chat and Anthropic use the old path, with an empty `forced`.
- `turn.rs`: `parse_request(OpenAiResponses)` uses `parse_strict_responses(.., Request)` and then `turn::responses`. `Malformed` gives `ToolTurn::Unavailable("malformed")`.
- F15: I deleted all 8 `allow(dead_code)` lines: 4 inner ones (classify, assembly, rewrite, body), 3 outer ones in json.rs, and 1 outer one in turn.rs. `git diff origin/main -- rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/src | grep -c "allow(dead_code)"` prints `0`.
- Mechanical test edits that the new variants force (F1): `Step::Terminal` added to the two test drivers of `openai/stream.rs` and `anthropic/stream.rs`. `Err(StepError::AfterEnd)` arms added to two Anthropic test helpers. An `unreachable!` arm added in one interceptor test that loops over chat and Anthropic only. No assertion changed.
- M2 measured no wire `output_text`, so I added no `output_text` notice and changed no spec text.

## Tests (all new)

- `stream.rs`:
  - `allow_all_reemits_every_payload_with_its_event_line`
  - `a_blocked_function_call_becomes_a_message_at_its_index`
  - `a_blocked_item_without_done_gets_a_synthesized_done` (terminal, EOF, `[DONE]`, `closing_on_abort`)
  - `an_abort_closes_a_rewritten_item_before_the_terminal_frame` (through `Interceptor::abort`)
  - `the_rewrite_repeats_the_sequence_number`
  - `a_truncated_item_blocks_the_whole_hold` (no `Decide`, two `Truncated` reports and notices)
  - `frames_after_the_terminal_are_dropped_and_done_is_emitted`
  - `an_oversized_record_after_the_terminal_is_dropped`
  - `provider_frames_wait_behind_an_open_hold`
  - `unframed_writes_a_safe_event_line` (`a\nb`, 65 bytes, uppercase, empty, a number, non-JSON, `[DONE]`; 64 bytes passes)
  - `known_calls_name_the_qualified_names` (`ns.f`, `srv.rm`)
  - `structured_output_keys_pass_on_the_stream` (§ 7.1)
  - `recorded_streams_pass_through_the_interceptor`
- `interceptor.rs`: `a_responses_stream_runs_end_to_end`, `the_chat_abort_bytes_do_not_change` (a Failed-mode blocked choice with an owed notice, and a truncated choice; each `abort` gives only `TERMINAL`).
- `body.rs`: `a_responses_body_parses_and_rewrites_through_parse_body` (it includes the F7 truncated-over-allow case in `apply` and in `report`), `structured_output_keys_pass_on_the_body`.
- `turn.rs`: `parse_request_reads_a_responses_request`.
- `assembly.rs`: `the_hold_is_cut_unless_a_terminal_event_completes_it`.

How I checked the recorded streams (D23, F6): `recorded_streams_pass_through_the_interceptor` reads all 17 `tests/fixtures/responses/recorded/*.sse`. It pushes each file through `Interceptor::new(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)` with the Responses limits (16 MiB record, 32 MiB held) and allow-all. For 15 files, the output without the report comments is byte-identical to the input file, and no record is dropped. For the two `*__max_output_tokens_in_call.sse` files, the test checks these facts:
- No `Decide` happens.
- The notice `tool call "write_file" was blocked (truncated).` is in the output.
- The frames before the call are unchanged.
- The call becomes exactly `output_item.added`, `content_part.added`, `output_text.delta`, `output_item.done`, and then `response.incomplete`.
- The terminal `output[0]` is `msg_paigasus_0`.
- `usage` is unchanged.

## Commands and results

- `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway-core`: 288 passed, 1 skipped.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`: clean. I touched `lib.rs` first, so that clippy checked the core and the gateway again.
- `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway-core --test golden` (no `UPDATE_GOLDEN`): 1 passed. `git status` shows no change under `tests/`.
- I did not run `SVC`. The task does not change the service, and clippy compiled it.

## TDD evidence

I did not follow the order of the brief. I wrote the implementation before the tests, so I have no RED run before the code. To show that the tests detect faults, I ran a mutation battery instead. The script is `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-core/1897327f-fffc-4b34-860d-d276c6197223/scratchpad/t6/mut.py`. It applies each mutation, runs `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway-core --lib --no-fail-fast`, and puts the file back from a copy (not `git checkout`). Every mutation compiled, and every mutation made tests fail (rc 100):

| Mutation | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| M1: no item rewrite | 8 tests, among them `a_blocked_function_call…`, `a_truncated_item…`, the recorded replay, and `a_responses_stream_runs_end_to_end` |
| M2: no owed `done` at the terminal | `a_blocked_item_without_done…` |
| M3: no `AfterEnd` | `frames_after_the_terminal…` |
| M4: `closing_on_abort` returns empty | `a_blocked_item_without_done…`, `an_abort_closes…` |
| M5a: a 65-byte event name allowed | `unframed_writes_a_safe_event_line` |
| M5b: `\n` allowed in an event name | `unframed_writes_a_safe_event_line` |
| M6: no terminal rewrite | 6 tests |
| M7: no oversized-after-terminal rule | `an_oversized_record_after_the_terminal_is_dropped` |
| M8: no forced code in the body | `a_responses_body_parses_and_rewrites_through_parse_body` |
| M9: `abort` ignores `closing_on_abort` | `an_abort_closes…` |
| M10: the terminal frame always touches the hold | `frames_after…`, the recorded replay |
| M11: a cut hold is decided | `a_blocked_item_without_done…`, `a_truncated_item…`, the recorded replay |
| M12: `parse_request` uses the chat profile | `parse_request_reads_a_responses_request` |

M9 first passed (rc 0). For that reason I added `an_abort_closes_a_rewritten_item_before_the_terminal_frame`, and after that M9 made it fail. GREEN: the full CORE run above.

## Files changed

- `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/src/responses/stream.rs` (new, 816 lines, about 210 of them code; the rest is tests)
- `src/protocol.rs`, `src/interceptor.rs`, `src/types.rs`, `src/body.rs`, `src/turn.rs`, `src/json.rs`
- `src/responses/{mod,assembly,body,classify,rewrite}.rs`
- `src/openai/stream.rs`, `src/anthropic/stream.rs` (test drivers only)

## Concerns

1. **A missing terminal event gives the code `Truncated`, not `Malformed`.** § 6.4 says that every deviation is `Malformed`, and R3 ("exactly one terminal event") is in § 6.4. This is a difference in the code label only:
   - When the stream ends at `[DONE]` or EOF with no terminal event, `hold_cut()` makes the hold incomplete, and the interceptor blocks every call with `Truncated` (or passes them under `on_failure = allow`). Every call is still blocked.
   - R15 names `[DONE]` and EOF with an open client-run item as a truncation. I used the same code when every item is done but the terminal event is missing, because D10 completes the hold only at the terminal event.
   - To get `Malformed` at EOF, the trait needs one more hook. The brief does not list one, so I did not add it.
   - With no hold open, a missing terminal blocks nothing and is not counted.
   - Please rule on it.
2. **The `sequence_number` of a synthesized `done`.** § 6.5 defines `<s>` as the number of the replaced frame. A synthesized `done` replaces no frame. I used the number of the item's `added` frame, so the key is present exactly when R7 says the stream has numbers. The spec does not say this.
3. **The stream checks no envelope numbers.** `check_numbers` runs only on the client-run items in the stream (`assembly::tool_call`), as the chat stream does. The body path calls `check_numbers_responses(.., Body)`, as the brief says. That check reads the whole `output[]`, provider-run items included, which is wider than F11 ("envelope and client-run items"). This scope comes from Task 3 and was accepted in its review. I did not change it.
4. **The rewrite under observe mode.** In observe mode (`on_failure = allow`) after a stream failure, the pass-through records are written by `unframed`. No owed `done` is synthesized before them. An owed `done` exists only when a block verdict came first, and under `allow` that happens only for a decider `Block` at the terminal event. By then the item has its `done`, so I see no real case.
5. **The file size.** `stream.rs` has 816 lines, and most of them are tests. `assembly.rs` was already 1787 lines (the Task 4 minor) and grew by the end-rule test.

  - `step`: R3 check first (after the terminal event, every record except `[DONE]` is `StepError::AfterEnd`, a malformed one too). Then `classify`. `[DONE]` gives `Step::End`. An error record gives `Step::UpstreamError`. A `Known` event goes to `Assembly::accept`. A terminal event gives `Step::Terminal`. Its `completed` list is `[(HoldKey::Response, hold_calls())]` only when the hold is open and not cut.
  - Touches: every frame of a client-run item touches `HoldKey::Response`. The terminal frame touches it only when the hold has opened. Without that condition, a response with no tool call waited for ever (the first test run showed it).
  - `release`: a frame with no blocked item keeps its payload bytes. It gets an `event: <data.type>` line (D11), and `[DONE]` gets none. A blocked item follows § 6.5: `added` gives the three events, middle frames are dropped, `done` gives the completed message. The terminal event gets the completed message at each blocked index. The notice for slot `s` is `notice_line(<qualified name>, code)`, and the names come from `Assembly::known()` (`display_name()`).
  - The synthesized `output_item.done` is written before the terminal frame, `[DONE]`, an error record, EOF (`closing`) and the D13 frame (`closing_on_abort`). Only an item whose rewritten `added` went out can owe one. A keepalive or a `response.audio.*` frame does not end the item. A later real `done` of an item that is already closed is dropped. The synthesized event repeats the `sequence_number` of the item's `added` frame, because no frame is replaced (see Concern 2).
  - `unframed`: writes an `event:` line only when `data.type` matches `^[a-z0-9_.]{1,64}$`.
  - `known_calls(Response)` gives `Assembly::known()`, with the qualified `<namespace>.<name>` names (the carry from Task 2).
- `protocol.rs`: `Step::Terminal { frame, completed }`, `StepError::AfterEnd`, and `Protocol::closing_on_abort` with a default body that returns `Vec::new()`.
- `interceptor.rs`:
  - `Format::OpenAiResponses` uses `ResponsesStream::with_cap(limits.max_held_bytes)`.
  - `Step::Terminal` completes the listed holds, then truncates `incomplete()`, then enqueues the frame.
  - `AfterEnd` counts `RecordDropped("after_done")`.
  - `abort` emits `closing_on_abort` before the terminal frame.
  - A new `after_terminal` flag makes an oversized record after the terminal event `after_done`, not a stream failure (the D4 hazard, applied to R3).
- `responses/assembly.rs`: the end-of-stream entry (the carry from Task 4). `ended()` reports that the terminal event arrived. `hold_cut()` holds the end rule: the hold opened and no terminal event completed it (R3, and R15 with an open item), or a truncation (R15), or an overflow (T4d). The stream decides only a hold that is not cut. A cut hold goes to `incomplete()`, and the interceptor applies `on_failure` to it, never allow. `sequence_numbers()` is now `#[cfg(test)]`, because only tests read it.
- `types.rs`: `Format::OpenAiResponses`.
- `body.rs`: `parse_body(OpenAiResponses)` uses `parse_strict_responses(.., Body)`, `check_numbers_responses(.., Body)`, `responses::body::calls`, and stores `responses::body::forced`. `BodyCalls::code` applies the forced code first, so a forced `Truncated` wins over the decider in `apply` and in `report` (F7).
